Commands:
  edit       Apply a patch document, read from stdin. See the `edit` MCP tool for the grammar.
  glob       Find files by glob, honouring .gitignore.
  grep       Search file contents, or piped input, by regex. Honours .gitignore.

  read       Read a text file as numbered lines under a 4-hex tag of its bytes.
  resolve    Show which server and workspace root a file resolves to, without starting anything.
  servers    List the configured language servers and whether each one is installed.
  write      Write a whole file, with content on stdin. Overwriting needs the tag from a read.

Usage: edit [options...] [-h|--help] [--version]

Apply a patch document, read from stdin. See the `edit` MCP tool for the grammar.

Options:
  -m, --mode <string>          atomic (all patches or none) or independent (apply what works). [Default: @"atomic"]
  --dry-run                    Validate and show the diff without writing.
  --retry <string?>            Token from a failed or dry-run batch, whose validated patches re-run. [Default: null]
  -r, --report <string>        auto | diff | summary | none. [Default: @"auto"]
  -C, --context-lines <int>    Lines of context around each changed region. [Default: 3]
  --cwd <string?>              Directory the section paths resolve against. [Default: null]
  --json                       Print the structured payload instead of the echo. Never elided.

Usage: glob [arguments...] [options...] [-h|--help] [--version]

Find files by glob, honouring .gitignore.

Arguments:
  [0] <string>    Glob, e.g. "*.cs" (any depth) or "src/**/*.cs" (path-scoped).

Options:
  -p, --path <string?>    Directory to search. Defaults to the working directory. [Default: null]
  -t, --type <string?>    Named type filter instead of a pattern, e.g. 'ts', 'py', 'config'. [Default: null]
  --hidden                Include hidden files.
  --by-modified           Sort by last modified. Implies a flat, ungrouped listing.
  --max <int>             Maximum files to return. [Default: 300]
  --format <string>       grouped | plain | auto. Auto is grouped on a terminal, plain when piped. [Default: @"auto"]

result.stdout:
Usage: grep [arguments...] [options...] [-h|--help] [--version]

Search file contents, or piped input, by regex. Honours .gitignore.

Arguments:
  [0] <string>      Regex to find. Use --fixed to match literally, as grep -F.
  [1] <string[]>    Files or directories to search, as grep takes them positionally.

Options:
  -p, --path <string?>     Directory or file to search. Omit to read stdin when it is piped. [Default: null]
  -g, --glob <string?>     Filter, e.g. "*.cs" (any depth) or "src/**/*.cs" (path-scoped). [Default: null]
  -t, --type <string?>     Named type filter, e.g. 'cs', 'ts', 'py', 'config'. Combines with glob. [Default: null]
  -F, --fixed-string       Match the pattern literally instead of as a regex.
  -i, --ignore-case        Force case-insensitive. Default is smart case.
  -s, --case-sensitive     Force case-sensitive. Default is smart case.
  -w, --word               Match whole words only.
  -v, --invert             Select lines that do NOT match.
  -l, --files-only         List matching files instead of lines.
  -c, --count              Print a count of matches per file.
  -C, --context <int>      Lines of context around each match (0-10). [Default: 0]
  --hidden                 Include hidden files.
  -m, --max-count <int>    Stop after this many matches per file, as grep -m. [Default: 0]
  --max <int>              Total matches to return across all files. [Default: 200]
  --format <string>        grouped | plain | auto. Auto is grouped on a terminal, plain when piped. [Default: @"auto"]

Usage: lsp [arguments...] [options...] [-h|--help] [--version]

Ask a language server about a position: hover, definition, references, and so on.

Arguments:
  [0] <string>    hover | definition | references | implementation | documentSymbol | workspaceSymbol | incomingCalls | outgoingCalls | diagnostics
  [1] <string>    Path to the file.

Options:
  -l, --line <int?>          1-based line number. [Default: null]
  -s, --symbol <string?>     Identifier on that line, e.g. "Push" or "Push#2". Preferred over --character. [Default: null]
  -c, --character <int?>     1-based column, when a symbol name cannot identify the position. [Default: null]
  -q, --query <string?>      Symbol to search for (workspaceSymbol only). [Default: null]
  --new-only                 Only diagnostics unseen since the last check.
  --project-dir <string?>    Pin the workspace root instead of detecting it. [Default: null]
